With long spikes crowning the frill at the back of its head, Styracosaurus is a magnificent herbivore dinosaur—like a cousin of Triceratops.

content.text:
Nature and science facts about Styracosaurus

Styracosaurus lived in North America about 75 million years ago and was up to 5.5m long. Its most striking feature is the 4-6 long spikes (each about 50-55cm) along the edge of its frill. These spikes could threaten predators, but they were most likely used for display. Fossils are found in Canada and the United States.

Points worth exploring together

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. How many frill spikes does Styracosaurus have?
A. 4-6, each about 50-55cm long. They were most likely used for display.

Q. Is it related to Triceratops?
A. Yes, they belong to the same ceratopsian (horned dinosaur) group. They're alike in having a frill and horns.

Q. How can we enjoy it at home?
A. Counting the frill spikes, comparing with Triceratops, and making a paper spike crown are all great.
